newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall after 2 straight records, on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall after 2 straight records, on rate worries.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks edged lower on Wednesday, after a string of two record closing highs, as investors once again fretted about interest rates and upcoming inflation data.
Wall Street braced for the Federal Reserve's "Beige Book" report on national business conditions due out at 2 p.m. EST on Wednesday.
"The Fed could raise rates pre-emptively on the basis of this report," said First Albany Corp. chief investment officer Hugh Johnson.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 6.54 points at 7,078.62. The index ended Tuesday at 7,085.16, beating Monday's record finish of 7,079.39.
In the broader market, declines led advancing issues by 14 to nine on volume of about 228 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond fell 3/32, which raised its yield to 6.86 percent from 6.85 percent at Tuesday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The Nasdaq Composite index, a barometer of high technology shares, was down 5.07 points at 1,311.69.
"The market is, basically, coming off its highs, and people are looking for any hint in the Beige Book of accelerated inflation," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"If that is the case, then the consensus view is that the Fed will launch a pre-emptive strike against inflation."
In addition, the February producer price index is due out on Friday, while the consumer price index is due out next Tuesday.
"The market has become very guarded since yesterday. After the February employment report, the feeling on the Street was that the Fed would not raise rates," Johnson said.
What changed this view, according to Johnson and other analysts, was an uptick in the fourth-quarter productivity and labour cost numbers released Monday.
"There is growing view that the Fed is likely to raise rates in March and even likelier to do so in May," he said.
The Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on March 25 and May 20.
"What every investors wants to do now is measure what the odds of a Fed hike are. The way they will try to do it is by looking at the Beige Book," Johnson said.
He said he believed the document would show that the economy had strengthened and that there was some upward pressure on wages in some of the Fed districts.
"What worries me is that the rally this year has been concentrated in a handful of Dow stocks," Westfalia's Cardillo said.
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co., said it was "more probable than not that the Fed will move next week on interest rates."
Among special situations, shares of Access Health Inc. were down 7-7/8 at 14-5/8 after the company said it expected fiscal year results to be below Wall Street consensus estimate.
The most actively traded NYSE issue was Advanced Micro Devices, up 5-5/8 at 47-3/8 after Prudential Securities raised its 12-month price target to $90 per share from $40 per share.
